hero.name: Deepak
hero.who: a bank branch manager in Nagpur, busy all day yet never feeling effective

story.b: Deepak's phone buzzes before his alarm. By the time he reaches the branch in Dharampeth at nine, he has answered eleven messages from the regional office. The day is a blur of loan files, a jammed cash machine, a customer shouting about a cheque and a meeting about targets. He eats poha standing up at four. He reaches home at nine, and his daughter Ananya, twelve, is already asleep, her science model half finished on the table. His wife Sunita reminds him he promised to help with it. He did. He meant to. On the weekend he plans to rest, but spends Sunday clearing emails. He feels busier than ever, and less useful than ever.

ask.q: Deepak works every hour and still feels he gets nowhere. What is the most useful first step for him?
o: Work longer hours until the pile is finally cleared
Step back and ask which few things truly matter at work and at home
Take a long holiday and hope things feel different afterwards
ask.why: More hours just feed the same pile, because the pile never ends. A holiday gives rest, but he returns to the same habits. Stepping back to see what truly matters lets him choose his work, instead of being pushed around by whatever shouts loudest.

chapters.take: Being busy is not the same as being effective.

story.b: A rumour spreads through the branch that it may be merged with the Sitabuldi branch next year. Lunch becomes a daily complaint session. Head office does not care, the targets are unfair, the new software is useless. Deepak joins in, and one afternoon he realises he has spent forty minutes on it. Not one sentence was about something he could change. That evening he writes two lists on the back of a deposit slip. One holds the merger, the targets and the software. The other holds his team's training, the morning queue and how he speaks to customers. The next week he spends lunch teaching his two new clerks the loan process, and the morning queue gets a token system.

ask.q: His clerk Pooja keeps worrying aloud about the merger and cannot focus. What should Deepak suggest?
o: Help her pick one skill or task she can improve this month
Agree that head office is unfair, so she feels understood
Tell her to ignore the news completely and stop thinking about it
ask.why: The merger is outside Pooja's control, so worrying about it drains energy without changing anything. Putting effort into a skill she can build makes her stronger whatever happens. Agreeing with complaints keeps her stuck there, and simply telling her to stop thinking rarely works.

chapters.take: Put your energy where you can act, not where you can only worry.

story.b: Deepak looks at his week and sees the problem. Everything urgent gets done. Nothing important does. His health check has been pending since March. He has not coached his team in months. Ananya's science model still sits half built. So on Sunday evening he opens his diary and blocks three things before anything else: a morning walk at Futala lake on Tuesday and Friday, an hour on Thursday to coach his team, and Saturday afternoon with Ananya. On Thursday at three, a regional manager calls asking for a report that is not due until Monday. Deepak feels the old pull to drop everything. Then he looks at the block in his diary.

ask.q: A report not due until Monday lands during Deepak's Thursday coaching hour. What should he do?
o: Cancel the coaching, because the regional manager asked personally
Do both at once, checking the report while his team talks
Keep the coaching hour and schedule the report for Friday morning
ask.why: The report feels urgent but is not due for days, while coaching builds a team that will lighten his load for months. Moving the report keeps both. Cancelling teaches him that every ping beats important work, and multitasking means neither gets done well.

chapters.take: Protect important work first, or urgent noise will eat every hour.

story.b: On Saturday, while they paint the solar system model, Ananya suddenly says she wants to quit the science club. Deepak's reply is ready in a second. Quitting is a bad habit, the club will look good later, she should not give up so fast. He opens his mouth, then closes it. He puts down the brush instead. He says it sounds like something about the club has been hard lately. Ananya goes quiet, then tells him the older girls laugh when she answers questions. She talks for ten minutes. He mostly nods. When she finishes, she asks him what he thinks she should do, and for once she actually waits to hear it.

ask.q: A customer storms into the branch, upset that his loan is delayed. What should Deepak do first?
o: Explain the bank's rules clearly so the customer sees he is wrong
Let him speak, then sum up his worry back to him before explaining anything
Promise the loan will be cleared tomorrow to calm him down
ask.why: People rarely listen until they feel heard. Summing up the customer's worry shows Deepak understands, and then his explanation lands better. Leading with rules sounds like a defence, and promising something he cannot guarantee will only damage trust later.

chapters.take: Listen until people feel heard. Then they are ready to hear you.

story.b: Deepak realises Sunita has stopped believing his promises. Too many missed dinners, too many times he said he would be home by eight. So he starts small. He tells her he will be home by eight on Wednesdays, and he is, every Wednesday, even when a file has to wait until Thursday. When he forgets to pick up her medicines once, he apologises plainly, without excuses. At the branch, two clerks are fighting over who works the second Saturday each month. Each keeps a list of past favours. Deepak sits with both and asks what each one actually needs. One has evening classes, the other a mother in Wardha. Together they build a rota that suits both.

ask.q: After months of missed dinners, Deepak wants Sunita to trust his word again. What will rebuild that trust best?
o: Make one grand gesture, like a surprise weekend trip
Explain in detail why work kept making him late
Make small promises and keep every single one, week after week
ask.why: Trust grows from many small kept promises, the way savings grow from regular deposits. A grand trip is one big gesture that the next missed dinner wipes out, and long explanations, however true, are words rather than proof. Steady small actions show Sunita his word is safe.

chapters.take: Trust grows from small promises kept, kindness shown and honest apologies.

story.b: One night Deepak cannot sleep. He sits at the dining table and writes three lines about the man he wants to be in ten years. A father Ananya talks to. A manager whose people grow. A body that can still climb the steps at Sitabuldi fort without stopping. Reading it back, he sees how far his days have drifted from all three. He also sees why he is always tired. No walks for a year, no books, no evenings with old friends. He adds a fourth line about looking after himself. A week later the regional office offers him charge of a second branch, with longer hours and a bigger title.

ask.q: Deepak is offered a second branch with longer hours and a bigger title. How should he decide?
o: Check the offer against his written lines and what it would cost his rest
Accept at once, because saying no could hurt his career
Refuse at once, because more work is always bad
ask.why: His written purpose gives him a clear test. If the role helps his people grow without taking every evening from Ananya and his health, it may fit. Saying yes by reflex lets others set his direction, and refusing by reflex skips the thinking. A clear purpose makes choices easier.

chapters.take: Know what you stand for, and keep recharging so you can live it.

story.b: By October, the merger has still not happened, and the branch has stopped talking about it. The token system has cut the morning queue in half, and Pooja now trains new clerks herself. Deepak still gets forty calls a day, but his Tuesday and Friday walks have survived three months, and his doctor was pleased at his last check-up. He took the second branch only after asking for a deputy, and he leaves at seven most days. On a Saturday in October, Ananya's solar system model wins second prize at the district fair. She tells the judges her father painted Saturn. Sunita, standing beside him, does not ask whether he will stay for the prize giving. She already knows.

chapters.take: Effectiveness means choosing what matters, again and again, until it becomes who you are.
